entities.name: Amr ibn Dinar
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Amr ibn Dinar (d. 744 CE) stands as a pivotal figure among the *tabi'un*, the generation of Muslims who succeeded the companions of the Prophet Muhammad, significantly shaping the nascent fields of Islamic jurisprudence (*fiqh*) and hadith transmission. Serving as the esteemed mufti of Mecca during the late Umayyad period, his legal opinions and rigorous methods of hadith narration were foundational for the development of Islamic law and scholarship. His life and work represent a critical juncture in the consolidation of Islamic intellectual traditions, bridging the direct teachings of the companions with subsequent generations of scholars.

Born into the vibrant intellectual milieu of early Islam, likely in Yemen before moving to Mecca, Amr ibn Dinar became a leading authority in the Hijaz. He transmitted hadith from numerous companions, including Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, and Anas ibn Malik, ensuring the preservation of prophetic traditions. His meticulous approach to narration, emphasizing direct auditory transmission (*sama'*) and careful verification, made his reports highly valued. As mufti, he issued legal rulings (*fatwas*) that addressed the practical concerns of the Meccan community and pilgrims, contributing to the evolving body of Islamic legal thought and setting precedents for future jurists.
